about: Shared-GLB asset manifest (docs/design/ASSET_PIPELINE.md). One entry per asset: the master GLB (PNG, what Godot imports) and the web variant (meshopt + WebP, what Three.js loads). files, tris, bounds_m, colliders and tools.gltf-transform/meshoptimizer/sharp are written by tools/assets/make-web-variant.mjs from the files on disk; the rest is written by hand from command output.

assets.name: Kit_Lot_Container20_01
assets.description: The Lot's 20 ft site-office container: open ends, a side door on +x 7 m toward +z (c_west; c_east is the same piece turned 180 degrees), windows, corner castings, hazard eaves band. Weathered corrugated steel, rust, grime, plywood floor.
assets.scale_note: World metres at the game's pet scale (x4): the body is CONTAINER in src/shared/world/lot/layout.ts, 9.6 x 10.4 x 24 m (a real 20 ft box, 2.44 x 2.59 x 6.06 m, x4); size_m adds the proud door leaf, rails and castings.
assets.axes: +Y up, front +Z (open end), pivot at the base centre on the ground

provenance.source: tools/assets/build-container.py + tools/assets/kitlib.py (bpy): geometry, LODs, COL_ boxes, UV atlas, painted textures (P-GLB1b: paint mask in the baseColor alpha; rust as edge wear + run-off streaks from drip sources), Cycles AO bake, glTF export. No .blend is kept; the scripts are the source.
provenance.web_variant: tools/assets/make-web-variant.mjs (glTF-Transform dedup, prune, textureCompress WebP q84 / normal q92, meshopt medium)
provenance.deterministic: two builds give byte-identical GLB and PNGs (sha256 in files)
provenance.generator_inputs: none: no image-to-3D model, no reference images, no paid API (Scenario / Grok blocked by the network policy)

assets.licence: Original work of the Corgis vs Cats project, generated by its own scripts; no third-party content.
assets.collision: COL_ boxes = the sim's container colliders (props.ts container()); tests/unit/glb-container-colliders.test.ts checks them within 1 cm against createWorldData('the_lot')

godot.master: PASS: editor import (--import) and runtime GLTFDocument both load it; tree root/LOD0-2/13 COL_, LOD0 AABB size (10.26, 10.46, 24.2) m on y = 0, StandardMaterial3D with albedo 1024x1024, normal, roughness, metallic and ao textures
godot.web: REJECTED: 'required extension EXT_meshopt_compression is not supported' and 'required extension KHR_mesh_quantization is not supported' (import and runtime). A WebP-only copy (no meshopt / quantization) imports and validates PASS, so EXT_texture_webp is fine; the meshopt geometry is the web-only part
godot.consequence: Godot imports the master (PNG) GLB; the web variant is Three.js-only, as ASSET_PIPELINE.md plans

assets.paint_mask: baseColor alpha: 1 = paint the game tints per instance (pbr({ paintTint }) via the per-instance paintTint attribute), 0 = rust, grime, frame, door, glass, floor; stored as 1 + 254 x mask (no texel at alpha 0, so a lossy WebP encoder keeps the colour underneath)

assets.name: Kit_Lot_BagWall_01
assets.description: One 4.8 m module of The Lot's cement-bag (sandbag) wall: two rows of woven sacks in running bond (row 0: two full sacks; row 1: a half, a full, a half), flattened under their weight, pinched at the tied ends; pale paper and canvas sacks, printed stencil band, mud on the lower row.
assets.scale_note: World metres at the game's pet scale: the section is props.ts bagWall()'s D x rows*BH = 1.6 x 1.1 m and the module two of its nominal 2.4 m sacks (read from props.ts). size_m adds the sacks' bulge. The game tiles m = round(len / 4.8) modules along each wall, stretched along z by len / (m x 4.8) (0.90-1.15 on The Lot).
assets.axes: +Y up; the wall runs along z (bagWall()'s own frame), +x is the printed face; pivot at the base centre on the ground

provenance.source: tools/assets/build-bagwall.py + tools/assets/kitlib.py (bpy): superellipsoid sacks with fold and wrinkle displacement, LOD0 5 x 16x12 / LOD1 5 x 8x6 / LOD2 one 8x4 hull per row, 1 COL_ box, one 512x256 atlas slot per sack (about 120 px/m), painted textures, Cycles AO bake (1.2 m), glTF export. No .blend is kept; the scripts are the source.
provenance.web_variant: tools/assets/make-web-variant.mjs (glTF-Transform dedup, prune, textureCompress WebP q84 / normal q92, meshopt medium)
provenance.deterministic: two builds give byte-identical GLB and PNGs (sha256 in files)
provenance.generator_inputs: none: no image-to-3D model, no reference images, no paid API (Scenario / Grok blocked by the network policy)
provenance.why: the Lot prop that most often stands next to the containers in the hero views: the two canyon-mouth walls 5.4 and 5.9 m off the containers' north ends are lot_container_canyon's foreground, three more walls are in lot_corgi_base (8 walls on the map)

assets.licence: Original work of the Corgis vs Cats project, generated by its own scripts; no third-party content.
assets.collision: one COL_ box per module = the sim's bags collider of a 4.8 m wall; tests/unit/glb-bagwall-colliders.test.ts tiles the modules along every Lot bag wall and checks their union equals each sim box within 1 cm

assets.name: Kit_Lot_Pipe_01
assets.description: One 9 m segment of The Lot's concrete drainage pipe (the Pipeworks tunnels, chapter 7's sneak route, and the two loose pipes in the Mud): a 12-sided tube with flat floor, crown and sides, outer rim chamfers; cast concrete with mould seams, spigot grooves, lifting anchors, lime run-off, algae and mud low down, a silted bore with a tide line, and an ochre spray arrow.
assets.scale_note: World metres at the game's pet scale: lot/pipes.ts addPipe() with layout.ts PIPE (ro 3.0 / ri 2.55 vertex radii, 12 facets, 9 m), read from the source. size_m is the outer facets' apothem x 2 (5.796) by the length.
assets.axes: +Y up; the pipe axis runs along z (the tunnels' heading; the loose pipes are turned pi/2); pivot at the base centre on the ground (the outer floor facet)

provenance.source: tools/assets/build-pipe.py + tools/assets/kitlib.py (bpy): the N-gon tube (LOD0 144 / LOD1 96 / LOD2 44 triangles: LOD2 is the barrel and a dark cap over each mouth), 12 COL_ facet boxes (4 box + 8 obb), a 1024 atlas of 11 faces (about 55 px/m outside, 34 in the bore), painted textures, Cycles AO bake (2.5 m), glTF export. No .blend is kept; the scripts are the source.

provenance.why: card item 1: the Pipeworks pipe section (8 placements: 6 tunnel segments + 2 loose pipes)

assets.licence: Original work of the Corgis vs Cats project, generated by its own scripts; no third-party content.
assets.collision: COL_ = the sim's 12 'pipe' facet boxes of props addPipe() (the 8 between the axes are oriented boxes, extras.collider = 'obb'); tests/unit/glb-lot-batch1.test.ts places them at every Lot pipe and checks all 96 boxes' corners within 1 cm, and that the bore lies inside lotInteriors()'s box of each pipe
assets.interiors: the bore is the exact inner 12-gon (apothem ri cos(pi/12) = 2.4631 m), mouth to mouth: every bore vertex lies inside its lotInteriors() box (W10 P5), and its floor, crown and both sides lie on the box's faces
assets.paint_mask: none: raw concrete, never tinted (no alpha)

assets.name: Kit_Lot_Footing_01
assets.description: The Lot's cast concrete footing block (the corgi base's Foundation): board-formed sides with bug holes, efflorescence and mud splash, a trowelled top with the oil stain and two lifting anchors, chipped arrises, and the two plywood formwork panels left on +-x with timber walers and tie-rod nuts.

assets.name: Kit_Lot_FloodMast_01
assets.description: The floodlight tower's standing half (props.ts floodTower()): the hazard-ochre ballast base with its checker plate and fork-pocket plates, the tapered gunmetal mast to the lamp bar with a base flange, gussets, a junction box, a conduit, step bolts and a collar.
assets.scale_note: World metres at the game's pet scale: the base 3.2 x 1.2 x 3.2 and the mast r 0.4 -> 0.3 up to FLOOD.mast = 22 m (read from props.ts / layout.ts). size_m adds the fork-pocket plates.
assets.axes: +Y up; square to the map (floodTower()'s base frame is yaw 0); pivot at the base centre on the ground

provenance.source: tools/assets/build-floodtower.py + tools/assets/kitlib.py (bpy): base, plates, mast in two 10.4 m halves, flange, gussets, junction box, conduit, 18 step bolts, collar (LOD0 484 / LOD1 118 / LOD2 34 triangles), 2 COL_ boxes, a 1024 atlas at about 94 px/m, painted textures, Cycles AO bake (2 m), glTF export. provenance.why: card item 2: the floodlight tower. It is two pieces because the world data turns the lamp bar to each tower's aim (yaw 1.50 / -1.13 / 2.81 / 3.14) and pitches the housings (0.73 / 0.67 / 0.87 / 0.90 rad) while the base stays square: one rigid GLB could equal none of the four towers' colliders. The lamp bar (a plain 6.4 x 0.4 x 0.4 box) stays procedural

assets.name: Kit_Lot_FloodLamp_01
assets.description: One sodium floodlight housing of the tower head: camo-black painted steel with a visor, side blinders, rear cooling fins, pivot bosses and a cable gland; a faceted polished reflector behind the lens.
